qt: to the Commission Marco Falcone (PPE), Fulvio Martusciello (PPE), Salvatore De Meo (PPE), Flavio Tosi (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Massimiliano Salini (PPE), Giusi Princi (PPE), Letizia Moratti (PPE) Subject:

Island regions in the European Union face specific challenges as a result of their unfavourable geographical location, and those challenges have a profound impact on territorial, economic and social development. Owing to their location, those areas face greater difficulties in the provision of essential services and the development of residents’ quality of life. In view of the above and, in particular, with a view to fostering island regions’ balanced and sustainable growth: 1.
With a view to upholding the principle of supporting islands, whose situation is different to that of mainland territories, what measures will the Commission take in the next financial programming?
What initiatives will it take to address island regions’ economic and social disparities, and are any specific measures to improve infrastructure and connections being provided for?
How will the Commission support island regions in their transition to a sustainable economy, also taking account of climate change?
at: (English version) to the Commission Marco Falcone (PPE), Fulvio Martusciello (PPE), Salvatore De Meo (PPE), Flavio Tosi (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Massimiliano Salini (PPE), Giusi Princi (PPE), Letizia Moratti (PPE) (26 November 2024) Subject: Fully honouring islands’ special situation in the EU Island regions in the European Union face specific challenges as a result of their unfavourable geographical location, and those challenges have a profound impact on territorial, economic and social development. Owing to their location, those areas face greater difficulties in the provision of essential services and the development of residents’ quality of life. In view of the above and, in particular, with a view to fostering island regions’ balanced and sustainable growth: 1.
With a view to upholding the principle of supporting islands, whose situation is different to that of mainland territories, what measures will the Commission take in the next financial programming?
What initiatives will it take to address island regions’ economic and social disparities, and are any specific measures to improve infrastructure and connections being provided for?
How will the Commission support island regions in their transition to a sustainable economy, also taking account of climate change?

(15 January 2025) EU islands are very diverse and face a variety of different challenges, including varying levels of economic growth and demographic trends. These different needs require tailor-made approaches, covering several EU policies. For example, EU Cohesion policy is designed to address EU regional economic and social disparities, including in island regions, in cooperation with Member States. Over the 2021-2027 programming period, the policy supports investments for increased competitiveness, innovation, green transition, better connectivity, and inclusive growth in all EU regions. In addition, Member States can use Cohesion policy territorial tools to address the particular needs of islands. The Commission also supports the ‘Clean energy for EU islands’ initiative (1) to promote and accelerate decarbonisation of islands’ energy systems and facilitate exchange of best practices. Furthermore, the EU's trans-European transport network (TEN-T) policy (2) incorporates the new overarching concept of a European Maritime Space, which aims to strengthen the integration of islands into the European Single Market and advance territorial cohesion. All of these lessons learned, will feed into the preparations for the post-2027 financial period.
